code: hb_blob_t *blob = hb_blob_create ((const char *)data, size, HB_MEMORY_MODE_READONLY, NULL, NULL);
note: The raw fuzzer input is accepted as an OpenType font byte blob without copying or semantic filtering.
The byte blob is wrapped as a face; later subset code reads table tags and table data through this face.
The fixed and input-derived codepoints determine which glyphs and dependent tables are retained during subsetting.
The harness invokes the subset implementation on the attacker-controlled face with both layout-retaining and layout-dropping modes.
User-influenced cmap/glyf data is traversed to populate the retained glyph vector used by later table subsetters.
Table enumeration from the malformed source face controls which table subsetters or copy paths execute.
Each retained table tag from the input reaches table-specific subset logic or the default table-copy path.
The destination face builder creates suppliers over the retained table entries after subsetting.
Serialization dereferences the retained table blob pointers and reads table bytes; malformed retained state can produce the sanitizer-reported stale stack read.
